I Should Have Bought The Unicorn Light

✦
✻

On being called "too practical," overthinking a six-year-old's birthday gift, and choosing wrong when I already knew right.

Haven't read the post yet? Start there →

The birthday girl's first question was: "Where's the present?"

I laughed and told her it was coming up in the lift with my husband.

Then my brain supplied the thought I really didn't need:

She's going to hate this.

Her mum had given me the brief: very girlish.

Unicorns. Kuromi. Rumi from KPop Demon Hunters.

Easy enough.

Except we had one day, and I am constitutionally incapable of buying anything without turning it into research.

The first thing I saw was an LED unicorn light.

I loved it instantly. We have unicorn lights at home. My boys climb on them more than they use them as lights. I took a photo and sent it to my husband, already convinced: done.

Perfect.

My husband called it "too practical."

Then came the second-guessing.

The shop was closing soon. I had every reason to decide quickly.

Instead, I walked away from the thing I had liked in ten seconds.

At Popular, the decision multiplied.

Books. Stationery. A school bag that cost 3.5 times the budget. Fifteen minutes of sending photos to my husband and vetoing each other's ideas.

Somehow, more options were making me less certain.

Meet every gift I considered → The Great Singapore Birthday Gift Pageant

I almost gave up when I passed the fiction section and gave it one last look.

There it was: Unicornia.

One title was A Magical Birthday.

Sensible. Relevant. Easy to wrap. Easy to defend.

So I bought it.

It doesn't open. It never does.

At the party, the present stayed wrapped.
Which meant I never had to watch her reaction. It also meant I never got an answer.

On the way home, the uncertainty followed me anyway.

At home, I finally said it out loud:

She would have loved that unicorn light.

I hadn't chosen the gift I believed in.
I'd chosen the one I could explain.

I should have bought the unicorn light.

✻

The light made me smile in under ten seconds.

The book made sense after fifteen minutes.

✦ Next time, the smile and the gut win. ✦
